newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia police rescue boy snatched by maids.
newsitem.headline: Colombia police rescue boy snatched by maids.

text.p: Crack anti-kidnap police rescued a 4-year-old boy in Bogota on Sunday after he was abducted five days ago with the help of two maids who worked at his home, police said.

Gen. Luis Gilbert, deputy chief of the national police, said the housekeepers, who had links with a criminal gang, planned the abduction and then told the boy's parents, identified only by their surname Galindo, that the house had been burgled.
The boy was freed after the police's GAULA squad, trained by Britain's Special Air Services (SAS), staged a dawn raid on a house in northern Bogota.

The NTC national TV news programme, meanwhile, reported another bizarre kidnap case in which the victim had been allowed to return home each night of his month-long ordeal so as not to arouse his family's suspicions.
Juan Gabriel Pacheco said his brother Jimmy, a taxi driver in the northeast city of Cucuta, had been abducted in December.

"The kidnappers sent him home every night to sleep while they watched from the street. Then in the morning he had to go back to where he was being held captive but we thought he was just leaving for work," Pacheco told NTC.
The taxi driver managed to escape from his daytime "prison" and raise the alarm at the weekend, NTC reported.
Colombia is the kidnap capital of the world. Last year 1,375 kidnaps were officially reported -- one every six hours and 20 minutes -- police said.
